The test image shows a **leaf** (appears to be the underside) with a pinkish-brown irregular lesion in the center and smaller pinkish clusters to the left. This narrows candidates to leaf diseases: Gray_Mold, Leaf_Mold, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Powdery_Mildew, Late_Blight, Early_Blight, etc.

The pinkish sporulation on the underside points strongly to Leaf_Mold or Gray_Mold. Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

Now I have enough data to make my assessment.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Plant part: **leaf** (underside, based on the dark green coloration and vein pattern)
- Central lesion: pinkish-tan/salmon, irregular angular shape, ~1-2cm, with some pale/white area in center
- Smaller pinkish-purple discrete spots to the upper left
- Otherwise healthy-looking dark green leaf

**Comparing to candidates:**

- **Leaf_Mold**: Underside shows olive-green to brown velvety sporulation in discrete spots. The pinkish-salmon color in the test image is close to this (color can shift in photos). Discrete bounded lesions on underside fit well.
- **Gray_Mold**: Shows large V-shaped tan blotches starting at margins — doesn't match the discrete central lesion.
- **Powdery_Mildew**: Shows white powdery spots on upper surface — color doesn't match the pinkish-brown.
- **Late_Blight**: White fuzzy sporulation, water-soaked brown lesions — the shape here is more discrete and bounded.

The discrete sporulation lesion on the underside of an otherwise healthy leaf, with the pinkish-olive velvety texture and satellite spots, best matches **Leaf_Mold** (Passalora fulva). The olive-brown spores can appear more pinkish-salmon depending on lighting and stage of infection.
